label: prf:sw-period-residue-sum
title: Proof that the Seiberg–Witten period is an algebraic residue sum
html:
By the MI--SW abelianisation, the n-th prolonged Seiberg--Witten differential \lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)} is the Cartan component of the abelianised connection on the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_c \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}). As a connection 1-form on a genus-zero curve it is meromorphic, with poles confined to the branch points z_c (the only points where the prolonged connection degenerates).

\mathcal{S}_c is compact, so \lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)} has finitely many poles p_1,\dots,p_k, all at branch points. For a cycle \gamma bounding a region whose poles are E \subseteq \{p_1,\dots,p_k\}, the residue theorem gives

\oint_{\gamma}\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)}
\;=\;
2\pi i \sum_{p_j\,\in\,E}\mathrm{Res}_{p_j}\,\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)},

the right-hand side being a finite sum of local residues. Identifying the left-hand side with the prolonged period a_D^{(n)} of prop:mi-sw-abelianisation gives the residue-sum shape: the period is computed by collecting residues, with no contour integration — once E is known.

Scope (corrected 2026-08-29, bean qou-6v5l). This argument previously ran over all k poles and appealed to "the period over the generating cycle of \mathcal{S}_c". Neither step is available. \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) has H_1 = 0, so there is no generating cycle; and the residue theorem on a compact Riemann surface states that the residues over all poles sum to zero, which would give a_D^{(n)} = 0 at every level rather than the positive binding period the keystone requires. The Lean records this as a derived consequence rather than a claim: QOU.Brings.period_eq_zero_of_total_residue_vanishes and its contrapositive total_residue_ne_zero_of_period_ne_zero, which is what forces E to be a proper subset. The companion witness QOU.Brings.sw_period_eq_residue_sum carries the residue-sum shape as an explicit hypothesis; it does not derive it.

A second, independent route reaches the same vanishing under the classical-jet rule: prop:sw-classical-jet-exactness shows \lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)} = d\bigl(X^{(n-1)}\bigr) is exact, so each residue vanishes on its own. That argument is stronger where it applies and is scoped to the classical-jet reading; the one here assumes only that the total vanishes, and is a property of the ambient surface rather than of the jet rule. \qquad\blacksquare
